tasks.description: Read in/emails.txt (one address per line). Write the domain part (after '@') of each, one per line, to out/result.txt.
Read in/times.txt (HH:MM durations, one per line). Write the integer total number of minutes to out/result.txt.
Read in/tags.txt (one line of ';'-separated tags). Write out/result.json: the JSON array of distinct tags in first-seen order.
Read in/users.json (array of objects with integer id). Write out/result.json: the JSON array of ids of objects that have no "email" key, in input order.
Read in/people.json (array of {id, age} with integer ages). Write out/result.txt with one line per record "<id> valid" if 0 <= age <= 150 else "<id> invalid".
tasks.expected:
p1 valid
p2 invalid
p3 invalid
p4 valid
p5 valid

tasks.description: Read in/ids.json (array of strings). Write out/result.txt: "ok" if all are distinct, else "duplicate:<id>" for the first id that repeats an earlier one.
Read in/schema.json (array of required key names) and in/config.json (object). Write out/result.json: the array of required keys missing from config, in schema order.

Read in/seq.txt (one integer per line). Write out/result.txt: "sorted" if the sequence is non-decreasing, otherwise "unsorted at <n>" where n is the 1-based line of the first value smaller than its predecessor.
Read in/items.json (array of {id, name}). Write out/result.json: an object mapping each id to its name.
Read in/profile.json ({user: {name, tags, ...}}). Write out/result.json: {"name": user.name, "tag_count": number of user.tags}.
Read in/members.json (array of {team, member}). Write out/result.json: an object mapping each team to the array of its members in input order.
Read in/records.json (array of objects). Write out/result.json: the same array keeping only the "id" and "status" fields of each object.
Read in/codes.json (object of string to string). Write out/result.json: the inverted object mapping each value to its key.
Recursively walk in/docs. Write out/result.txt containing the integer number of regular files under it.
Recursively walk in/docs. Write out/result.txt with the paths (relative to in/docs, '/'-separated) of all files ending in .txt, sorted lexicographically, one per line.
